CHANDRESH SHUKLA S/O P.R.SHUKLA, AGED  ABOUT 37 YEARS, NEAR OF SHASTRI BRIDGE,
 NAPIER TOWN, JABALPUR (MADHYA PRADESH)
 (OWNER OF CAR NO.MP20-CA-6920)
 .
 (BY SHRI ARPAN PAWAR - ADVOCATE FOR ESPONDENTS NO.1 TO 4)
 T h is appeal coming on for orders this day, t h e cou r  following:
 ORDER

This miscellaneous appeal is filed under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 being aggrieved of award dated 19th August, 2016 passed by learned 4th Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Katni in Claim Case No.106/2015 on three grounds.

entities.text:
4th Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Katni
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Firstly, FIR was lodged against unknown vehicle.
Within two days vehicle was seized and it was implanted.
2. Second ground is that the income tax had not been deducted from notional income of the deceased who was working as a Sub Engineer.

Third ground is that three children of the deceased-Premlal Chandore are major, therefore, learned Claims Tribunal has erred in making deduction of 1/4 towards the living expenses of the deceased whereas it should have been 1/2.
3. Shri Arpan Shrivastava, learned counsel for respondents No.1 to 4/claimants, supports the award.

However, he submits that since no cross objection is filed but in the interest of justice and with a view to do complete justice, he submits that High Court of Bombay in Kelkar and Kelkar Vs. Shripad Narayan Gore and Others, 2019 SCC OnLine Bom 4140 has held that there is no restriction to enhance compensation in appropriate case even in absence of cross-appeal or cross-objection.

entities.text: Kelkar and Kelkar Vs. Shripad Narayan Gore and Others, 2019 SCC OnLine Bom 4140
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Similarly, reliance is placed on the judgment of Supreme Court in Jitendra Khimshankar Trivedi and others Vs. Kasam Daud Kumbhar and others, (2015) 4 SCC 237, wherein it is held that it is the duty of the Court to determine just and reasonable compensation.

entities.text: Jitendra Khimshankar Trivedi and others Vs. Kasam Daud Kumbhar and others, (2015) 4 SCC 237
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Same is the ratio of judgment of the Supreme Court in Mona Baghel and others Vs. Sajjan Singh Yadav and others, 2022 LiveLaw (SC) 734, this Court can show indulgence.

entities.text: Mona Baghel and others Vs. Sajjan Singh Yadav and others, 2022 LiveLaw (SC) 734
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 4. After hearing learned counsel for the parties, as far as implant of vehicle is concerned, no evidence is led by the insurance company.
FIR (Ex.P/3) is on record.
Thereafter investigation was carried out, vehicle was seized on 25/3/2015.
Number of vehicle has come on record as M.P.20 CA 6920.
No connection could be shown between the seized vehicle and the deceased or his family by the insurance company.
In fact insurance company did not examine any witness to deny the aspect of accident taking place with the said vehicle bearing registration No.M.P.20 CA 6920.

Independent The Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. vs Smt. Ranu on 13 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141036022/
2 witness Manoj Barman was examined who proved the factum of accident.

entities.text: Independent The Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. vs Smt. Ranu on 13 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This evidence could not be rebutted in cross-examination.
Thus, first ground in regard to false implication is concerned, is not made out.
5. Second ground in regard to income tax has substance.
6. As far as third ground of deduction living expenses is concerned, the submission made by Shri Gulab Sohane, learned counsel for the appellant is misplaced and contrary to law.

Even if wife could have been the only claimant, then also 1/3rd deduction should have been made and not 1/2 as suggested by Shri Sohane, learned counsel, in terms of the law laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sarla Verma & Ors Vs. Delhi Transport Corp. & Anr. (2009) 6 SCC 121 .

entities.text: Sarla Verma & Ors Vs. Delhi Transport Corp. & Anr. (2009) 6 SCC 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Therefore,
learned counsel for the insurance company has not appreciated the law laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in correct prospective and is making inappropriate submission.
7. It is settled law that merely because children have grown up, it does not mean that their dependency on the father will make over.
In view of such facts when there are four dependents, then making 1/4th deduction cannot be said to be illegal or arbitrary.
8. As far as plea of income tax is concerned, that has some bearing.
Income of the deceased is accepted by learned Tribunal to be Rs.53,179/- per month or Rs.6,38,148/- per annum.

As per the slab of income tax applicable on the date of accident i.e. 03/02/2015, income upto Rs.2,50,000/-
was exempted from the income tax.
Then remaining of Rs.2,50,000/- tax @ 10% is applicable that comes out to Rs.25,000/- and on the remaining tax is applicable @ 30%.
Salary slip of the deceased is available on record.
a sum of Rs.4,000/- was deducted towards GPF.
That amount of GPF and Rs.400/- towards GIS is deductable under Section 80 of the Income TAx Act.
Thus, a sum of Rs.50,800/- will be deducted from the salary of the deceased.
It has come on record that a sum of Rs.1,000/- was being deducted towards income tax and that has already been deducted by learned Claims Tribunal while making computation.
Thus, total income tax comes out to Rs.42,070/-.
After deduction of income tax, net income will come out to Rs.5,96,078/-.
1/4th is to be deducted towards living expenses of the deceased, that will come out to Rs.4,47,058.50.
15% is to be added towards future prospects in light of the law laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi in AIR 2017 SC 5157.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi in AIR 2017 SC 5157
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thereafter multiplier of 9 will be applicable and when applies, then take total pecuniary compensation to Rs.46,27,055/-.
Besides this, Rs.1,25,000/- under the head of non-pecuniary compensation, taking total compensation to the tune of Rs.47,52,055/- against a sum of Rs.43,31,249/-.
Thus, there will be enhancement to the tune of Rs.4,20,806/- which will be admissible in favour of the claimants.
The enhanced amount shall carry interest @ 6% per annum from the date of filing of claim petition till the date of actual payment.
Other terms and conditions of the award shall remain intact.
9. In above terms, this appeal is disposed of.
10. Record of the Claims Tribunal be sent back immediately.
